rulings.evidence: Fresh raw sausage sold by the pound with casings to remove; smoked-turkey-sausage is a fully cooked rope at a different price class and italian-sausage is pork. No commodity claims it today, so a new id is proposed.

Ground basil is the same dried-herb jar as dried basil, same price class; only the grind differs, so I weighed it denser (2 tsp ground about 2.8 g against 1.4 g of leaf). Fresh basil is refused - different price and different weight.
Same call as basil: ground vs leaf is a grind within one spice-jar SKU, priced 7/7; weighed at the denser ground figure.

Whole seed and ground fennel are the same spice in the same size jar at the same price; minting a `fennel-seeds` id would duplicate a commodity already priced 5/7, which is exactly the yellow-mustard/mustard trap.
"Crushed" is part of the product's own shelf name, not a form flip - crushed red pepper and red pepper flakes are one jar.
Aged Italian hard cheese sold as its own wedge/shred SKU; parmesan, provolone and ricotta are different cheeses at different prices, and no commodity claims asiago today.
Same 8-count bun pack and same price class as the priced `hamburger-buns` id; whole wheat is a within-SKU variety here, not a form flip, and no separate bun premium exists to price. 43 g per bun.

new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Fresh raw turkey sausage, refrigerated and sold by the pound with casings intact. Not already priced under another name: `smoked-turkey-sausage` is the fully cooked rope/kielbasa format (ready-to-eat, different price per lb), `kielbasa` is the pork version of that same format, and `italian-sausage` is pork. Board reports no commodity claims it while today's captures do carry matching products, so it is priceable, just unnamed.

Aged Italian hard cheese sold as a wedge or a shred cup in the specialty case. Checked by food, not string: parmesan, provolone, ricotta and mozzarella all exist as their own ids and none of them is asiago; no romano/parmesan-blend id covers it. Captures carry matching products today, so this is a naming gap, not a carriage gap.

registrar_rulings.reason: Already priced under a longer name the mapper's case skipped: fresh-sweet-italian-turkey-sausage [commodities.json line 69843] is fresh raw cased turkey sausage sold by weight — same food, same form as the proposal — live in smp-feed.json at $0.30/oz (Walmart, Honeysuckle White Sweet Italian Turkey Sausage, fresh links), and for italian-turkey-burgers the Italian-style fresh sausage is precisely the intended purchase; a generic turkey-sausage include would match the identical products and mint the 80-20-ground-beef-style duplicate. Follow-up: add recipe-floor-id-map.json pair turkey-sausage -> fresh-sweet-italian-turkey-sausage (both weight-based, units match); do NOT mint a new id. The rows the mapper did rule out (smoked-turkey-sausage, kielbasa, italian-sausage=pork) are correctly different form or different animal. Vocabulary side, kept separate: the ingredient NAME 'turkey sausage' has no ingredients.json row shown — if intake needs one, mint the name resolving to this id, no new id alongside it.

Genuinely unpriced: no asiago id in any of the three namespaces, no price cell in smp-feed.json, no recipe-floor-id-map pair, and the estate's ONLY 'asiago' string is inside pecorino-romano's EXCLUDE list (commodities.json:67101) — the estate already treats asiago as a distinct cheese it does not carry, so this is a naming gap, not a hidden spelling (parmesan, pecorino-romano, provolone, gruyere, feta, block/shredded/sliced-cheese all checked and none is asiago). Mint in the recipe namespace (recipe-board-everyday baseline + recipe-commodities.json for sale overlay), unit oz. Prescription: include patterns like '\basiago(?:\s+cheese)?\b' with V4-grade excludes (~150, model on pecorino-romano's list) — mandatory: asiago BAGELS/bread, asiago dressing/dip/spread, parmesan-asiago and romano-asiago BLENDS, cheese crisps/snack cups, prepared pasta/pizza, pet/baby items. Add commodity-dupe-allowlist.json pair asiago-cheese vs parmesan ('different hard Italian cheeses; pecorino-romano already excludes asiago') so the audit never re-flags it. Vocabulary side, separately: no ingredients.json row and no macros row exist — mint the NAME 'Asiago cheese' and transcribe a label; the FDC hits offered (cream-cheese spread, cheese bread) are the wrong food, use none of them.

macro_cross_check: Source publishes 690 cal / 33 carbs / 53 protein over 6 servings. Recomputed at source scale from the rows above: about 675 cal and 53.5 g protein per serving (turkey 115/14.2, sausage 117/14.2, mozzarella 115/8.9, asiago 135/9.5, bun 116/5.3, olive oil 40, panko 12, vegetables 20). Calories -2%, protein +1% - the closest match in this batch, so no portion is re-examined. Carbs recompute to about 30 g against the published 33, inside the 35 g cap but with little headroom: the bun alone is 19 g, so any bun swap moves the recipe against the condition.
